# expr

> `deepnoodle/expr` is a small, zero-dependency expression language for Go
> programs. It compiles a line of Go-flavoured expression syntax once and
> evaluates it repeatedly against any env (map, struct, or pointer to
> struct). It is intended for embedding conditions, templates, and
> parameter interpolation inside a larger Go program — not as a general
> scripting language.

This file is a condensed reference aimed at LLM context windows. Human
readers should start with [`README.md`](README.md); the authoritative
language reference is [`docs/reference/spec.md`](docs/reference/spec.md).

## Mental model

- **Expressions only.** No statements, no `:=`, no `if`/`for`, no blocks,
  no function definitions. An expression takes an environment and
  produces a value.
- **Parsed by `go/parser.ParseExpr`.** The accepted grammar is a strict
  subset of Go expression syntax, with two ergonomic extensions: bare
  `[...]` becomes `[]any{...}` and bare `{"k": v}` becomes
  `map[string]any{"k": v}`.
- **Walked, not compiled.** expr visits the `ast.Expr` directly. There is
  no bytecode, no VM, no optimizer. This is deliberate — the whole
  library is ~3.9k non-test Go LOC.
- **Safe by default.** `MaxSourceLength` (64 KiB) caps the parser;
  `MaxEvalDepth` (256) caps the evaluator. Bitwise ops, pointer ops,
  channel ops, spread args, type assertions, and function literals
  are all rejected at eval time.
- **Loosely typed at runtime.** Integers are `int64`, floats are
  `float64`, numeric comparisons mix freely, and truthiness covers
  nil/false/zero/empty-string/empty-collection.

## Installing

```sh
go get github.com/deepnoodle-ai/expr
```

## Minimal program

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/deepnoodle-ai/expr"
)

func main() {
    p, err := expr.Compile(
        `user.age >= 18 && contains(user.roles, "admin")`,
        expr.WithBuiltins(),
    )
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    env := map[string]any{
        "user": map[string]any{
            "age":   36,
            "roles": []any{"admin", "editor"},
        },
    }

    v, err := p.Run(context.Background(), env)
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Println(v) // true
}
```

`Compile` parses once. The returned `*Program` is immutable and safe to
share between goroutines. `Run` takes a `context.Context` and the env.

## Options

Options are applied in order; later options override earlier ones for
any shared name.

| Option                                | Effect                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `expr.WithBuiltins()`                 | Registers the standard builtin function set (see below)   |
| `expr.WithFunctions(map[string]any{})`| Registers arbitrary Go functions as callable identifiers   |

Builtins are opt-in: if you don't pass `WithBuiltins`, the only callable
names are the higher-order forms (always registered) and anything you
registered yourself. This keeps the sandbox surface as narrow as you want.

## Builtin functions (opt in via `WithBuiltins()`)

| Name              | Signature                      | Notes                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `len(v)`          | `(any) -> int`                 | Runes for strings; elements for slice/array/map/chan      |
| `string(v)`       | `(any) -> string`              | Passthrough; cycle-safe `%v`-style formatting otherwise   |
| `int(v)`          | `(any) -> int64`               | Truncates floats; rejects NaN/Inf/out-of-range; strict base-10 strings |
| `float(v)`        | `(any) -> float64`             | `strconv.ParseFloat` 64-bit for strings                   |
| `bool(v)`         | `(any) -> bool`                | Same rules as truthiness                                  |
| `contains(h, n)`  | `(any, any) -> bool`           | Substring, element, or map-key presence                   |
| `has(m, k)`       | `(any, string) -> bool`        | Key presence on a map (nil → false)                       |
| `keys(m)`         | `(any) -> []any`               | Sorted string keys                                         |
| `upper(s)`        | `(string) -> string`           | `strings.ToUpper`                                          |
| `lower(s)`        | `(string) -> string`           | `strings.ToLower`                                          |
| `sprintf(f, ...)` | `(string, ...any) -> string`   | `fmt.Sprintf`-style; cycle-safe for recursive values      |

## Higher-order forms (always registered)

The second argument is a predicate AST that is re-evaluated per element
with `it` (current element) and `index` (0-based position) in scope.
These shadow any outer identifier of the same name. `list` must be a
slice, array, or nil (maps are not iterated — drive with `keys(m)` if
you need to).

| Form                  | Returns          | Description                                           |
| --------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `map(list, expr)`     | `[]any`          | Transform every element                               |
| `filter(list, pred)`  | `[]any`          | Keep elements matching predicate                      |
| `any(list, pred)`     | `bool`           | True if any match (short-circuits)                    |
| `all(list, pred)`     | `bool`           | True if all match (empty list → true, short-circuits) |
| `find(list, pred)`    | element or `nil` | First match or nil                                    |
| `count(list, pred)`   | `int64`          | Number of matches                                     |

Names can be shadowed by `WithFunctions` or an env entry of the same
name. The literal token `map` is rewritten to an internal sentinel
before parsing (Go treats `map` as a keyword), then translated back for
error messages.

## Custom functions

```go
p, _ := expr.Compile(`greet(upper(name))`, expr.WithFunctions(map[string]any{
    "upper": strings.ToUpper,
    "greet": func(name string) string { return "Hello, " + name + "!" },
}))
```

Supported return signatures: `T`, `(T, error)`, and `()`. Anything else
errors at call time. Variadic functions are supported; spread syntax at
the call site (`f(xs...)`) is not.

**Automatic context injection.** If the registered function's *first*
parameter is `context.Context`, expr passes the live `ctx` from `Run`
automatically. The caller-visible call surface excludes that parameter:

```go
expr.WithFunctions(map[string]any{
    "fetch": func(ctx context.Context, url string) (string, error) { ... },
})
// called from expr as: fetch("https://...")
```

## Environment kinds

`env` can be:

- `map[string]any` — identifiers are map keys. Missing keys are
  **errors**, not zero values.
- Any other map with string-like keys (`reflect.String`, including
  named string key types) — resolved via reflection.
- Struct — exported field, falling back to zero-arg bound method of
  the same name. Fields beat methods. Unexported fields are unreachable.
- Pointer to struct — dereferenced and retried. Nil pointer is an error.
- `nil` — only functions and higher-order forms resolve.

```go
p, _ := expr.Compile(`Subtotal() > 100 && len(Items) >= 2`, expr.WithBuiltins())
v, _ := p.Run(ctx, order) // struct or *struct with a Subtotal() method
```

## Templates

```go
t, _ := expr.NewTemplate(
    `Hello ${user.name}! You have ${len(user.tasks)} task(s).`,
    expr.WithBuiltins(),
)
out, _ := t.Render(ctx, env)
```

Each `${...}` is compiled once at construction time and re-evaluated on
every `Render`. Outside of `${...}` the template text is literal.

## JSON-style literals

Bare `[...]` and `{"k": v}` are rewritten before parsing into
`[]any{...}` and `map[string]any{"k": v}`. Strings, runes, comments, and
typed Go composite literals are left alone.

```go
{"items": [1, 2, 3], "count": 3, "ok": true}
```

Only `[]any` and `map[string]any` composite shapes are accepted at eval
time. `[]int{1, 2}`, `[3]int{}`, struct literals, etc. all parse but
error at run time.

## Multi-line expressions and semicolon insertion

expr reuses Go's parser, which means Go's automatic-semicolon-insertion
rule applies inside expression source. When an expression is split
across multiple lines, every continuation line **must end with an
operator, comma, or opening bracket** — never with an identifier,
literal, or closing `)` / `]` / `}`. The safe continuations are
`&&`, `||`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`,
`,`, `(`, `[`, `{`. Multi-line call arguments can use trailing commas.
See `docs/guides/examples.md` for worked multi-line expressions.

## Loose semantics worth remembering

- **Equality (`==`, `!=`)** is loose: mixed int/float kinds compare as
  `float64`; typed nil values compare equal to literal `nil`; mismatched
  types are `false` without error; uncomparable types error.
- **Arithmetic:** int+int → int64; integer overflow and division/modulo
  by zero error instead of silently wrapping or panicking. Any float mix
  → float64; `+` on strings is concatenation.
- **Truthiness:** nil, false, zero numbers, empty string, empty
  slice/array/map, and typed-nil nilable kinds are falsey. Everything
  else is truthy.
- **Short-circuit:** `&&` / `||` short-circuit on truthiness. `cond && "msg"`
  returns the string when cond is true, which is the expr idiom for
  "emit this value if the condition holds."
- **String indexing** counts runes, matching `len` on strings.
- **Selectors and index errors:** missing map keys, missing struct
  fields, nil selectors, and out-of-bounds indexes all return
  `ErrEvaluate` — expr never panics on well-formed env input.

## Errors

All parse failures wrap `ErrCompile`. All runtime failures wrap
`ErrEvaluate`. User function errors returned from `(T, error)` signatures
are wrapped so `errors.Is` and `errors.As` still find the original cause.
Unknown identifiers, fields, and keys get a Levenshtein-based
"did you mean...?" hint drawn from what's actually in scope.

```go
if errors.Is(err, expr.ErrCompile) { /* ... */ }
if errors.Is(err, expr.ErrEvaluate) { /* ... */ }
```

## Cancellation

`Program.Run(ctx, env)` checks `ctx.Err()` before dispatching each AST
node. A cancelled or expired context causes the next node to return the
raw `context.Canceled` / `context.DeadlineExceeded` without wrapping, so
callers can match with `errors.Is`. Registered functions that block on
I/O should accept a `context.Context` as their first parameter — expr
injects it automatically.

Go has no way to kill a goroutine, so a registered function that ignores
its context and blocks forever cannot be interrupted. This is by design;
expr will not silently leak goroutines to make cancellation look nicer.

## What is *not* supported

These parse but error at eval time, so the "did I use a feature expr
doesn't have?" answer is always readable:

- Slice expressions (`x[a:b]`, `x[a:b:c]`)
- Type assertions (`x.(T)`)
- Bitwise operators (`& | ^ << >> &^`)
- Pointer/address ops (`*x`, `&x`)
- Channel ops (`<-ch`, `ch <- v`)
- Imaginary literals (`1i`)
- Spread call arguments (`f(xs...)`)
- Composite literals with any type other than `[]any` or `map[string]any`
- Function literals (`func() {}`)
